prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Reform UK’s “Contract” frames Britain as broken by Conservative rule and threatened by Labour, citing high taxes, debt, mass immigration, crime, Net Zero costs, and failing public services. It claims Brexit’s opportunities are unrealised and offers a “common sense” alternative focused on border control, law and order, tax cuts, energy self‑reliance, cultural conservatism and sweeping institutional reform.

Core pledges
- Freeze non‑essential immigration; stop small boats.
- Zero NHS waiting lists while remaining free at point of use.
- Make work pay: raise income tax threshold to £20,000.
- Cut energy bills by scrapping Net Zero and green levies; expand domestic oil and gas.

Immigration and borders
- Freeze non‑essential migration; essential health skills exempt.
- Four‑point plan: leave ECHR, no UK resettlement for illegal entrants, create a Department of Immigration, return small boats to France.
- Detain and rapidly process illegal arrivals (offshore if needed); bar asylum/citizenship from safe countries; no legal aid for non‑citizens.
- Immediate deportation of foreign criminals; revoke citizenship for serious crimes.
- Bar student dependents; close “fake” courses; five‑year residency to access benefits.
- Employer immigration tax: raise NI to 20% for foreign workers (exempt essential health/care, firms ≤5 staff).

Spending and economy
- Stop paying interest on QE reserves; 5% efficiency saving across departments; cut foreign aid by 50%; deregulate retained EU laws; improve HMRC collection.
- Personal tax: lift threshold to £20k; higher rate at £70k; cut fuel duty by 20p; scrap VAT and levies on energy; big stamp duty cuts; restore VAT‑free tourist shopping; abolish IHT below £2m (20% above).
- Business: exempt SMEs up to £100k profit from corporation tax; cut main rate to 20% then 15%; abolish IR35; raise VAT threshold to £150k; abolish business rates for high‑street SMEs (4% online delivery tax); planning reform; easier hiring/firing; tax simplification.

Public services and law/order
- NHS: zero basic‑rate tax for NHS/social care staff (3 years); end training caps; student loan write‑offs for service; use independent capacity; 20% tax relief on private health; voucher guarantees for GP/consultant/operation waits; efficiency drive; Pharmacy First; inquiry into excess deaths.
- Policing/justice: recruit 40,000 officers; zero‑tolerance policing; expand stop/search; tougher drug and knife crime penalties; scrap DEI roles; redefine hate crime; add 10,000 prison places; mandatory life for violent repeat offenders; youth training camps; tougher action on grooming gangs.

Education, families, benefits
- Patriotic curriculum; ban transgender ideology in schools; 20% tax relief on independent school fees; scrap student loan interest; tighten degree entry and numbers; enforce free speech; more exclusions; two‑year degrees.
- Family: transferable marriage allowance (25%) when affordable; front‑loaded child benefit; single‑sex spaces; child‑safe phones.
- Benefits: “make work pay,” two‑strike job offer rule, face‑to‑face assessments.

Energy, infrastructure, other sectors
- Scrap Net Zero and renewables subsidies; fast‑track North Sea and shale; later SMRs, other tech.
- Scrap HS2; ban ULEZ/LTNs; no ICE bans; boost regional transport; 50% public/50% UK pension‑fund ownership of utilities; cap standing charges.
- Defence to 2.5% GDP by year 3, 3% by year 6; pay rises; veterans department.
- Housing: fast‑track brownfield; prioritise locals in social housing; restore mortgage interest relief for landlords; drop Renters’ Reform Bill; leasehold protections.
- Agriculture: increase budget to £3bn; scrap climate‑linked subsidies; buy‑British targets.
- Fisheries: restrict foreign access, license fees, ban supertrawlers; rebuild processing.
- Social care: Royal Commission; tackle offshore tax practices.

Constitution/culture
- Leave ECHR; reform Lords and civil service; tighten postal voting; PR referendum; British Bill of Rights; scrap BBC licence fee; reject WHO treaty/WEF influence/CBDC; anti‑corruption unit; St George’s and St David’s Days as holidays.

Funding
- Claimed savings: ~£160bn/year (incl. £10bn from extra growth) versus costs of £141bn/year, mainly from efficiency, QE interest, scrapping Net Zero, welfare reforms, foreign aid cuts, and an employer immigration tax.
